messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts for customer CobaltAnalytics on Dedicated cluster dc-west-3. Error rate spikes starting at ~2026-11-03T10:13Z. Routing: dedicated-pool-dc-west-3 -> affected. Paging oncall@sara.

sara (oncall): saw the alert, joining. thanks for the page. pulling logs now. can someone confirm if this is tenant-scoped or pool-wide?

jamal (infra): I'm seeing a huge backpressure signal on the kube nodes hosting dedicated-pool-dc-west-3. Pod CPU/IO for tenant=cobalt looks normal-ish but total open connections + accept queue is high. probable noisy neighbor or connection leak.

meera (eng-runtime): getting the same 502/504 gateway errors from gateway-proxy logs. snippet: ```[2026-11-03T10:14:02Z] upstream response timeout for request id=xyz status=504 backend=worker-27 tenant=cobalt```. KV cache pressure increased, eviction thrash on a few workers.

ivan (customer success): customer reports ~12% of requests failing, mostly during peak batch windows. they're seeing user-facing failures on their app. I told them we're investigating and will update in 15.

ops-bot: automatic mitigation suggestions: 1) isolate tenant via pool-affinity override 2) temporarily enable rate-limiting on tenant 3) scale up pool by +2 workers 4) route overflow to hosted fallback model. Use `/incident-apply` to run.

sara (oncall): immediate plan: 1) throttle cobalt to 10r/s per-route 2) move cobalt to isolated nodepool (if possible) 3) scale pool by +1 now, +1 if persists 4) prepare fallback route to `hosted-small` model variant. Jamal/meera you ok to run? I'll own customer comms.

jamal (infra): running nodepool scale +1 now. command: ```gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize rigs-dc-west-3 --size=15``` -> started, ETA ~2min to attach. also flagging to evict long-lived conns: `kubectl exec -n dedicated kube-proxy -c connctl -- ./connctl --evict --tenant cobalt` (dry-run first).

meera (eng-runtime): enabling per-tenant throttling on the router: ```PATCH /config/router
{ "tenant": "cobalt", "max_rps": 10 }``` applied. starting to route new requests to fallback after 10s drain. Turning on KV cache aggressive eviction for this tenant.

sara (oncall): customer notified: "We're seeing elevated errors and actively mitigating — temporary rate limits and routing fallbacks applied. We'll update in ~10-15m." ivan ack?

ivan (customer success): sent update to CobaltAnalytics NOC and assigned a follow-up call if they want. they asked for ETA; I gave ~15m.

ops-bot: nodepool resize completed, 2 new workers attached. health checks passing.

meera (eng-runtime): after throttling+scale: error rate dropped from 12% -> 3.4% over 90s. latency p50 unchanged, p95 improved ~400ms. Worker logs still show occasional 502s tied to long tails on requests with large seq lengths.

jamal (infra): I see one host worker-27 with sustained high iowait and many slow epoll/accept syscalls. marking worker-27 for restart and draining connections. `kubectl drain worker-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> draining.

sara (oncall): good. restart and monitor. also keep the throttles until we confirm stable.

meera (eng-runtime): restarted worker-27; after restart its metrics are normalizing. KV cache hit-rate dipped because of eviction, but overall throughput recovered.

ivan (customer success): customer reports errors falling to single-digit percentage. appreciative of rapid action. asking for root cause timeline.

jamal (infra): preliminary: noisy tenant within the same pool had a connection storm (unexpected long-poll worker jobs + massive concurrent prefix queries) causing backpressure and accept-queue saturation on a subset of hosts. eviction/isolating + scale mitigated. we'll follow up with more detailed metrics.

meera (eng-runtime): evidence: stack traces show repeated large-seq generation (seq_len>1024) attempts for cobalt during their batch window, causing KV cache thrash. Also saw repeated grpc stream re-establishes from the same client IP block. Suspect client retries + large payloads.

sara (oncall): status update to channel: mitigation in place, customer impact reduced, oncall will monitor for 30m. next steps: postmortem draft, follow up with cobalt for request pattern and possible client-side rate limiting. If errors remain above 1% after 30m -> escalate to P0.

meera (eng-runtime): adding follow-up actions: 1) add per-tenant connection limits + backoff guidance to docs 2) improve router backpressure signals to more proactively reject instead of queuing 3) create alert for per-tenant KV eviction rate.

jamal (infra): we'll also add a script to detect accept-queue depth anomalies per-host and auto-evict the top offending tenant for X minutes.

ivan (customer success): scheduling a post-incident call with CobaltAnalytics on their preferred window. will include our suggested mitigations and ask for client-side adjustments.

sara (oncall): handing off monitoring to jamal for next 30m, I'll keep watch but logging off for a meeting in 10. Jamal, please ping here if anything regresses.

jamal (infra): ack taking over monitoring. setting watches: `alert if tenant_error_rate(cobalt) > 2% for 5m` and `host_accept_queue > 100 for any host`.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved for now. final metrics: peak error rate 12.1% at 10:14Z, reduced to 1.8% by 10:23Z after throttling+scale+worker restart. total customer errors ~14k requests failed. follow-up: postmortem assigned to eng-runtime + infra, severity P1.

sara (oncall): thanks team. I'll create the incident ticket and link metrics/dashboards. can someone capture the exact queries/log lines for the postmortem before we close?

meera (eng-runtime): I'll export the KV eviction and gateway logs and attach to the ticket.

ivan (customer success): closing loop with customer: they'll expect a postmortem and recommended client changes.

jamal (infra): monitoring looks stable at T+40m. handing back to oncall rotation.

incident-bot: this thread will be archived to incidents log. reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:
